name: glass_plate
description: Render the footage under one item (normally an overlay) as small blurred frames, one JPEG per frame, for frosted glass. An overlay is captured in its own page and composited afterwards, so CSS backdrop-filter in it sees nothing; a glass shape shows the plate frame of the current frame instead, positioned at screen coordinates. The plate is the project's video and image tracks only (never overlays or captions), drawn by the export's own render path for the item's range at project fps, so transforms, crops, speed and the HDR-to-SDR look already match the export. Plate frame n is the screen frame under the overlay's frame n; gaps with no footage are black. Draw it at the design canvas size (canvas) shifted to screen coordinates. It lines up only when the overlay item drawing it is full-canvas, with no offset, scale, rotation or keyframes on the item, and only the video and image tracks are in it: an opaque overlay underneath is not. Returns { frames: [absolute paths], fps, size: [w, h], canvas: [w, h] }, one frame per project frame in the item's range: round(end * fps) - round(start * fps). canvas is the overlay design canvas (1080 on the short edge, the aspect of settings.resolution), the size to draw a plate frame at.

input.description: The project id, its folder, or the absolute path of its project.json

output.description: { frames: [absolute JPEG paths, 0000.jpg on], fps: project fps, size: [w, h] of the frames, canvas: [w, h] of the overlay design canvas }

params.name: project
params.description: The project id, its folder, or the absolute path of its project.json

params.name: item
params.description: Id of the item the plate is for, normally the overlay item. Its start and end set the range. Any item in the project is accepted; an unknown id is an error.

params.name: short-edge
params.description: Short edge of the plate in px; the long edge keeps the project's aspect. Both are rounded to even.

params.name: sigma
params.description: Gaussian blur sigma in plate pixels (2.2 at 270 is about 8 px at 1080). 0 writes the frames unblurred.

params.name: sdr-curve
params.description: Look curve id for the HDR-to-SDR grade (see montaj_assets/luts/looks.json: 'natural1', the default; 'vivid1'; 'vivid1-neutral'), as render's --sdr-curve. Omit to use the default look.

params.name: out
params.description: Folder for the frames. Defaults to <project_dir>/plates/<item>/ (an item id with a path separator or a colon needs an explicit out). Never a root, the home folder or a folder holding it. The new frames are written aside and replace the NNNN.jpg frames in it only once all are written, so a failed run keeps the previous plate; nothing else in the folder is touched.
